title: Authentication for API Clients
keywords: choosing authentication based on the threat model
subtopics: Choosing authentication based on the threat model.
learning_outcomes: Explain what authentication for api clients contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: api keys.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: API integrations cross a network boundary where responses can be slow, malformed, unauthorized, duplicated, or unavailable. Check status and content, set timeouts, and make retries and webhook processing safe to repeat. In this lesson, focus on api keys; then compare it with bearer tokens. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use authentication for api clients when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: API integrations cross a network boundary where responses can be slow, malformed, unauthorized, duplicated, or unavailable. Check status and content, set timeouts, and make retries and webhook processing safe to repeat. For authentication for api clients, begin with api keys. Also distinguish bearer tokens; oauth 2.0 concepts; token expiration and rotation. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
